decided_by: Malcolm picked SKIN8-reclining-sweep-nbp_flash_02 from the skin-art round-3 batch for /pages/faq; then asked for a taller band so more of the frame shows; then: keep the band the same height as every other page, but show more of the image
note:
Header banner for /pages/faq. This FILLS AN EMPTY SLOT rather than replacing anything: the hero section existed with no image at all and `overlay_opacity: 100`, so the page has been rendering a solid black band with the heading on it.

SOURCE: brand-band skin-art round 3, SKIN8-reclining-sweep, Nano Banana Flash candidate 02. Class B, no product in frame. Same pose family as the /pages/skin-concerns header, which took nbp_pro_02 from the same slot — a different candidate, so the two pages share a register without repeating a picture.

CROPPED, NOT EXTENDED. The band measures 1920x440 live, needing 4.364:1, and the source is 2.357:1. 1236px of 2688 comes off, leaving 6336x1452 at 4.364:1 with nothing invented.

THE CROP OFFSET IS THE WHOLE DECISION HERE, because this frame has no dark zone and the heading is CENTRED. Measured across candidate bands, the text zone — middle 46% wide by middle 30% tall — reads 117.9 at the top of the frame and 120.4 in the middle, both far too bright to carry white type. At top=1224 it reads 54.7. The frame runs bright at the top-left and falls away to the bottom-right, so the bottom band is the only one where a centred heading has any ground at all.

OVERLAY 100 -> 25. At 100 the image is invisible, which is what the page does today. 25 matches the research pages and leaves the skin its warmth; 40 was tested and reads duller for no legibility gain the crop had not already won.

MOBILE: the phone band is 1.048:1. Six crops were measured and the centre — where the heading sits — ranged from 150.6 down to 49.0; the crop at left=3515 is the darkest by a wide margin and keeps the face and throat. It also gets a CENTRE-WEIGHTED scrim rather than an edge one, because the heading sits in the middle of the phone band: 5% at the frame edges rising to 42% at the centre. Heading zone goes from mean 54.8 / max 236 to 39.7 / 153, while the top of the crop stays at 96.3 and the bottom at 16.2 — the skin keeps its range instead of being flattened.

OPTIMISATION: capped at 3000 on the long edge, quality 95, 4:4:4, metadata stripped, and not compressed harder — the CDN re-encodes to WebP and a pre-compressed source hands it artefacts to reproduce.

IMAGE_SIZE sm -> md, 2026-08-25, on Malcolm's request for more of the image in the band. The theme's heights are responsive and measured off theme.css: sm 375/400/440, md 480/460/500/560, lg 560/560/640/720. At a 1920 viewport that makes the band 4.364:1 at sm, 3.429:1 at md and 2.667:1 at lg, against a 2.357:1 source — so cover keeps 54%, 69% and 88% of the source height respectively.

md was chosen over lg on the text, not on the picture. lg shows most of the frame but its centred text zone measures 97.8 against md's 66.4 — the heading would sit on lit skin — and a 720px header would stand far taller than every other header on the store. md keeps the whole shoulder-to-jaw sweep with the face in frame and still gives the heading ground.

The master was REBUILT rather than reused: the sm master is 4.364:1, and dropping it into a 3.429:1 band would have cropped 21% off the WIDTH instead. New crop is 6336x1848 from top=840, chosen the same way as before — the darkest centred text zone across candidate bands.

THE MOBILE BAND CHANGED SHAPE WITH THE SIZE, which is easy to miss: at sm the phone band is 393x375 (1.048:1) and at md it is 393x480 (0.819:1), noticeably portrait. The 1.048:1 phone crop would have lost 22% of its width to cover, so it was rebuilt at 0.819:1 with the same centre-weighted scrim.

REVERTED TO image_size sm, AND THE CROP WAS THE REAL PROBLEM ALL ALONG. Malcolm asked to keep the band the same height as every other header and still show more of the frame, which forced a correction to my own earlier reasoning.

What decides how much of the SOURCE a visitor sees is not the band height but the MASTER's aspect, because object-fit cover crops whichever axis is surplus. Cropping the master to 4.364:1 up front — so that it would fill a 1920 band with nothing left over — threw 46% of the source away permanently, and then showed that same 54% at every viewport. Feeding the band the UNCROPPED 2.357:1 source instead lets it crop for itself, and the visible fraction becomes source/band: 81% at 1280, 72% at 1440, 54% at 1920. Better or equal at every width, with no change to the band.

I was optimising for the master filling the band, when the objective was the source filling the eye.

Anchored BOTTOM with a page-scoped object-position rule, because the crop is now the theme's to make and the bottom of this frame is the only part dark enough to carry a centred white heading. Text zone with overlay 25 reads 47.3 at 1920, 58.9 at 1440, 68.4 at 1280 — the widest screens, which show least, get the darkest ground.

Mobile returns to the 1.048:1 crop, since the phone band goes back to 393x375 at sm.
